sources.title: Configure the connector for any CRM solution
Set up the embedded experience in Salesforce
Contact center with existing CRM and CCaaS
Create rollout plans to manage AI agents
Best practices for application lifecycle management
Migrate configurations for channels using solutions
Copy an environment with omnichannel capabilities
Manage personas and custom security roles
Control user access with security groups and licenses

questions.prompt: An engineer manually loads accounts from a retained CRM into Dataverse. The flow succeeds, but only the first page of a much larger account set arrives. Later incremental updates work. Which change addresses the incomplete initial load?
questions.answer: Enable pagination for the initial-load connector operation.
questions.explanation: Treat historical loading separately from later event delivery. Pagination addresses the missing initial pages.

options.text: Recreate the incremental webhook subscriptions.
Change the initial-load trigger from manual to scheduled, retaining the same page retrieval.
Enable pagination for the initial-load connector operation.
Rerun the first-page request with a narrower account filter.

optionExplanations.o1: Incremental notifications do not fetch omitted historical pages.
optionExplanations.o2: Trigger timing does not retrieve the omitted historical pages.
optionExplanations.o3: Pagination retrieves records beyond the connector fetch page.
optionExplanations.o4: Narrowing the requested account set does not complete the required full initial load.

questions.prompt: A one-time CRM account import is complete. Contact Center must now react to source create, update, and delete events rather than depend on periodic full reloads. The CRM exposes webhooks. Which design meets this requirement?
questions.answer: Deliver source changes through CRM webhooks to flow endpoints.
questions.explanation: Use incremental event delivery for ongoing changes; a complete initial load is a separate milestone.

options.text: Deliver source changes through CRM webhooks to flow endpoints.
Schedule periodic full imports without subscribing to source change events.
Increase initial-load pagination without configuring source change notifications.
Subscribe only to new-record notifications and use the completed initial load for later edits and deletions.

optionExplanations.o1: Webhooks notify flows about source record changes.
optionExplanations.o2: A full-import schedule does not provide the required event-driven change delivery.
optionExplanations.o3: Paging completes batch retrieval, not ongoing event delivery.
optionExplanations.o4: Create-only notifications omit the required update/delete events.

questions.prompt: Two retained CRM systems contain contacts with identical display names. The integration design must preserve which source record each Dataverse contact represents and provide a route back to that record. Which TWO design choices follow the connector prerequisites? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Store the originating CRM in Source CRM. Preserve Source CRM ID and Source CRM URL on each synchronized record.
questions.explanation: Keep both source-system identity and the source record reference in the documented account/contact columns.

options.text: Use display name as the only source identity.
Store the originating CRM in Source CRM.
Replace Source CRM ID whenever the contact name changes.
Preserve Source CRM ID and Source CRM URL on each synchronized record.
Store the source CRM only on a flow configuration record and omit source identity from synchronized contacts.

optionExplanations.o1: Names are not stable source-record identifiers.
optionExplanations.o2: This identifies the originating system.
optionExplanations.o3: A name edit should not replace source record provenance.
optionExplanations.o4: These columns preserve source identity and navigation.
optionExplanations.o5: Flow-level metadata does not preserve the documented source-record columns on each contact.

questions.prompt: A deployment has the required connector solution and account/contact columns. The engineer built the Power Apps setup in the service environment but selected a separate sandbox for Power Automate. Before diagnosing credentials, which prerequisite should be corrected?
questions.answer: Use the same Power Apps and Power Automate environment.
questions.explanation: Check environment alignment before treating this cross-environment setup as a connector authentication defect.

options.text: Grant the flow owner more CRM permissions.
Reinstall the connector in the sandbox.
Recreate the Dataverse connection in the sandbox and keep the Power Apps setup elsewhere.
Use the same Power Apps and Power Automate environment.

optionExplanations.o1: Additional privileges do not correct environment alignment.
optionExplanations.o2: Reinstallation leaves the documented environment mismatch.
optionExplanations.o3: A connection recreation in the wrong environment does not fix alignment.
optionExplanations.o4: The connector prerequisite requires matching environments.

questions.prompt: The embedded conversation widget works for the Salesforce administrator who performed setup. Another intended representative uses the same Service Console and has the required Contact Center access. The call-center definition and default softphone layout are correct. Which Salesforce configuration should be checked for this user?
questions.answer: Check the representative call-center membership.
questions.explanation: Validate the per-user Salesforce call-center association after the shared definition and layout are configured.

options.text: Reimport the shared call-center XML.
Check the representative call-center membership.
Change the default layout for everyone even though that shared setting is verified.
Replace the adapter URL used by all users even though it works for the administrator.

optionExplanations.o1: Reimporting shared configuration does not address the missing individual association.
optionExplanations.o2: The documented setup adds the intended user through Manage Call Center Users.
optionExplanations.o3: The question states the shared layout is correct.
optionExplanations.o4: The adapter is already verified; user association is the remaining specific check.

questions.prompt: The Salesforce call-center definition, adapter URL, intended user membership, and default softphone layout are verified. The representative can use the embedded widget in a configured Salesforce app but does not see it in Service Console. Which Service Console application configuration should the engineer inspect?
questions.answer: Add Open CTI Softphone to the Service Console Utility Items.
questions.explanation: Embedding includes application-level softphone setup as well as call-center configuration.

options.text: Add Open CTI Softphone to the Service Console Utility Items.
Reimport the shared call-center definition without reviewing Service Console configuration.
Change the existing default softphone layout without reviewing application Utility Items.
Reassign the user to the already verified call center without changing Service Console Utility Items.

optionExplanations.o1: This adds the documented application-level utility.
optionExplanations.o2: The verified shared definition does not establish the utility for this application.
optionExplanations.o3: The shared default layout is already verified; its presence does not configure the console utility.
optionExplanations.o4: Membership is verified and does not add the required application utility.

questions.prompt: An organization selects the documented architecture that retains both its CRM and its CCaaS provider while adding Copilot for Service and Copilot Studio. During the design review, who should remain responsible for routing and post-conversation operational supervision?
questions.answer: The existing CRM and CCaaS services retain those operational responsibilities.
questions.explanation: Keep the documented architecture boundary: adding assistance does not transfer retained-provider routing and supervision duties.

options.text: Copilot Studio automatically replaces both services when an agent is published.
A new Dynamics unified-routing deployment is an inherent requirement of this architecture.
The existing CRM and CCaaS services retain those operational responsibilities.
The embedded Copilot component becomes the authoritative routing and supervision service.

optionExplanations.o1: Self-service automation does not replace all provider operations.
optionExplanations.o2: This retained-provider architecture does not inherently replace its routing service.
optionExplanations.o3: The architecture assigns routing, follow-up and supervision to the retained providers.
optionExplanations.o4: Assistance inside CRM does not itself own these operational services.

questions.prompt: A project plans the documented Salesforce embedded conversation experience. System requirements, the widget URL, representative membership, and the console utility are already verified. Which TWO remaining checks belong to readiness before representative acceptance testing? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Verify omnichannel capabilities are enabled. Verify a softphone layout is selected as default.
questions.explanation: Check the underlying contact-center service and the Salesforce softphone default, rather than treating a visible utility as full readiness.

options.text: Reimport the call-center definition and treat that alone as proof the service and layout are ready.
Verify omnichannel capabilities are enabled.
Grant all consuming representatives Salesforce System Administrator, matching the provisioning user.
Verify a softphone layout is selected as default.
Keep the intended softphone layout nondefault because adding a console utility implicitly makes it default.

optionExplanations.o1: A definition import does not establish omnichannel provisioning or the default layout.
optionExplanations.o2: The underlying service must be provisioned.
optionExplanations.o3: The provisioning-user permission does not imply all consuming representatives need that role.
optionExplanations.o4: The documented layout must be selected as default.
optionExplanations.o5: The setup separately requires selecting the default layout; the utility does not remove that step.

questions.prompt: A team is configuring its workspace acceptance test. A representative accepts a customer conversation and then opens that customer record from the conversation session. What behavior should the test expect?
questions.answer: Open a tab in the current conversation session.
questions.explanation: Sessions preserve interaction context; related customer records can open as tabs within the active session.

options.text: Replace the conversation with Home.
Open a new independent session and move the existing conversation into it.
Close the conversation session before the related customer record can be opened.
Open a tab in the current conversation session.

optionExplanations.o1: Related record navigation does not replace the conversation with Home.
optionExplanations.o2: The documented behavior is a tab within the existing session.
optionExplanations.o3: The workspace supports opening customer context without closing the conversation.
optionExplanations.o4: This preserves that conversation session context.

questions.prompt: A test lead proposes using the agentic simulation preview as the sole acceptance test for an English inbound voice journey that requires callers to press keypad digits to choose a branch. What is the appropriate assessment?
questions.answer: Use a separate keypad test; simulation preview excludes DTMF.
questions.explanation: A supported inbound voice channel does not establish keypad coverage. Keep this preview limit explicit in the acceptance plan.

options.text: Accept it because it uses an inbound voice workstream.
Use a separate keypad test; simulation preview excludes DTMF.
Accept it after describing each keypad press explicitly in a more detailed English prompt.
Select a DTMF-enabled receiving workstream.

optionExplanations.o1: Inbound voice scope alone does not establish DTMF support.
optionExplanations.o2: The preview does not support keypad interaction.
optionExplanations.o3: Prompt detail cannot supply an unsupported simulation feature.
optionExplanations.o4: A receiving workstream capability does not change the simulation limitation.

questions.prompt: After a supported agentic simulation preview run, the lead needs both the exact submitted prompt with run status and the conversation transcript with recording. Which TWO places supply that evidence? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Simulation Run History for the submitted prompt and run status. The closed conversation form for transcript and recording.
questions.explanation: Use run metadata and conversation artifacts together; neither is a substitute for the other.

options.text: Simulation Run History for the submitted prompt and run status.
The closed conversation form as the authoritative history of the exact simulation request prompt.
The closed conversation form for transcript and recording.
The Ongoing conversation report as the permanent source of the submitted simulation prompt.
The run status alone, without opening the conversation, as evidence of its exact dialogue.

optionExplanations.o1: Run History supplies the simulation request and status.
optionExplanations.o2: The documented submitted-prompt location is Run History.
optionExplanations.o3: The form supplies the dialogue artifacts.
optionExplanations.o4: Live monitoring does not replace the required prompt/status history.
optionExplanations.o5: Completion status does not show what the conversation said.

questions.prompt: An administrator has provisioned voice and configured a workstream number for the agentic simulation preview. To test that workstream, which number should the administrator include in the natural-language simulation prompt?
questions.answer: The intended receiving workstream number.
questions.explanation: Distinguish the receiving workstream number from the caller number supplied by the simulation service.

options.text: The previous simulated caller number.
A representatives callback number.
The intended receiving workstream number.
An unassociated spare test number.

optionExplanations.o1: The simulation supplies the caller identity, not the destination.
optionExplanations.o2: This does not identify the receiving workstream.
optionExplanations.o3: The prompt identifies the receiving workstream number.
optionExplanations.o4: An unassociated number does not address the configured receiving journey.

questions.prompt: A validation team has completed all documented simulation-preview prerequisites. It must choose one initial journey that falls within the published channel, direction, and language scope; none uses keypad input. Which candidate can be exercised within that scope?
questions.answer: An English inbound voice journey using a simulation-configured receiving number.
questions.explanation: Select a supported journey before interpreting its run as validation evidence: the preview scope is English inbound voice.

options.text: An English outbound voice callback journey through the campaign dialer.
A French inbound voice journey handled entirely through spoken dialogue.
An English website live-chat journey with the same escalation rules as voice.
An English inbound voice journey using a simulation-configured receiving number.

optionExplanations.o1: The preview scope is inbound voice, not outbound calls.
optionExplanations.o2: The documented simulation language is English only.
optionExplanations.o3: The preview is for voice, not website chat.
optionExplanations.o4: This candidate meets the documented inbound voice and English scope.

questions.prompt: A Contact Center administrator has the documented access role and working billing setup. Service Operations Agent previously performed supported requests, but now cannot retrieve environment information or perform actions. Before changing operational configuration, which documented connection dependency should the administrator verify?
questions.answer: Verify the environment Dataverse MCP connection.
questions.explanation: Investigate the documented environment connection when supported retrieval and action requests fail together.

options.text: Verify the environment Dataverse MCP connection.
Configure Application Insights and assume monitoring supplies the agents Dataverse management connection.
Grant broader representative data roles without checking the administrators existing Dataverse connection.
Point the existing connection to another environment and assume it will manage the intended environment.

optionExplanations.o1: The agent requires this connection for environment access.
optionExplanations.o2: Application Insights is a troubleshooting prerequisite, not the required MCP connection to access and manage Dataverse.
optionExplanations.o3: The administrator access role is verified; new representative grants do not verify the failing connection.
optionExplanations.o4: The agent must connect correctly to the intended environment, not another one.

questions.prompt: An organization has Service Operations Agent access, consumption-based billing, and its Dataverse MCP connection working. It now wants the documented troubleshooting capability during setup. Which TWO additional observability checks are required? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Configure Application Insights. Connect Application Insights with Dynamics 365 Contact Center.
questions.explanation: Monitoring provisioning and the Contact Center connection are separate prerequisites for this troubleshooting path.

options.text: Refresh the already working Dataverse MCP connection and treat that as Application Insights setup.
Grant the administrator source-table export privileges without configuring a monitoring service.
Configure Application Insights.
Grant broader Dataverse read privileges and skip connecting monitoring to Contact Center.
Connect Application Insights with Dynamics 365 Contact Center.

optionExplanations.o1: A working environment-management connection does not configure the separate monitoring prerequisite.
optionExplanations.o2: Table export access does not provide Application Insights configuration.
optionExplanations.o3: Application Insights must be configured.
optionExplanations.o4: Broader read access is not the documented monitoring-service connection.
optionExplanations.o5: The configured monitoring service must be connected to Contact Center.

questions.prompt: An administrator uses Service Operations Agent to create a route-to-queue rule. The rule must now check a customer-tier condition. Existing queues and the workstream use the same channel. How should the condition be added under the documented tool support?
questions.answer: Configure the condition manually in Copilot Service admin center.
questions.explanation: Separate supported rule creation from unsupported condition authoring; use the manual configuration path for the latter.

options.text: Ask the agent to convert the rule to percentage-based distribution.
Configure the condition manually in Copilot Service admin center.
Grant the agent a broader role.
Change the queues assignment method.

optionExplanations.o1: Percentage-based distribution is also outside the tools and does not express this condition.
optionExplanations.o2: Adding or editing rule conditions requires the manual administration path.
optionExplanations.o3: This is a capability boundary, not a documented missing privilege.
optionExplanations.o4: Queue assignment strategy does not author a route condition.

questions.prompt: An authorized deployment lead is planning a phased Customer Intent Agent rollout for a new business scope. Which sequence follows the documented relationship between autonomous-agent setup and rollout-plan creation?
questions.answer: Enable the autonomous agent, then create the plan.
questions.explanation: Rollout manager uses existing enabled agent configurations; it does not remove the enablement prerequisite.

options.text: Create and Schedule the plan first, relying on its future lifecycle action to perform agent setup.
Create an inactive plan first and use Activate to replace enablement of the underlying agent.
Enable the autonomous agent, then create the plan.
Create a plan using another enabled agent and assume its rollout activates the intended agent too.

optionExplanations.o1: Scheduling a plan does not replace the prerequisite enabled agent configuration.
optionExplanations.o2: Plan activation is not a substitute for the documented agent prerequisite.
optionExplanations.o3: Agent enablement precedes plan creation.
optionExplanations.o4: The intended selected agent must satisfy its own enablement prerequisite.

questions.prompt: An enabled agent has an approved rollout plan. The business wants the plan enabled automatically at a specified future date and time without an administrator returning then. Which plan action meets this requirement?
questions.answer: Schedule.
questions.explanation: Use the plan lifecycle action that explicitly supports future automatic enablement.

options.text: Schedule.
Edit the approved scope while leaving the plan inactive and without a schedule.
Activate immediately and rely on the future business date to delay the effect.
Deactivate the plan and expect it to reactivate automatically at the requested time.

optionExplanations.o1: Schedule supplies automatic future enablement.
optionExplanations.o2: Edit changes plan settings but does not provide the requested future automatic enablement.
optionExplanations.o3: Activate is immediate rather than the requested scheduled action.
optionExplanations.o4: Deactivation alone does not supply a future activation schedule.

questions.prompt: An operator is preparing to deactivate one Customer Knowledge Management Agent rollout plan and one Case Management Agent rollout plan. Which TWO effects must the operator account for? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: The knowledge agent setting remains after plan deactivation. The corresponding Case Management Agent rules are also deactivated.
questions.explanation: Plan deactivation has agent-specific effects; verify the underlying settings or rules instead of assuming a universal stop behavior.

options.text: The knowledge agent setting is always deleted with its plan.
The knowledge agent setting remains after plan deactivation.
Case Management Agent rules remain active regardless of plan deactivation.
The corresponding Case Management Agent rules are also deactivated.
All unrelated agents are automatically disabled.

optionExplanations.o1: The documentation says this agent setting is not deactivated or deleted with the plan.
optionExplanations.o2: The underlying knowledge agent setting persists.
optionExplanations.o3: Case Management Agent has the documented rule lifecycle coupling.
optionExplanations.o4: Its corresponding rules are deactivated with the plan.
optionExplanations.o5: The documented effect is agent-specific, not an organization-wide disable.

questions.prompt: Two enabled autonomous agents will be adopted together under one business rollout. Their individual configuration remains on the corresponding administrator pages. Which approach fits rollout manager without creating a second configuration authority?
questions.answer: Use one multi-agent rollout plan and the existing settings.
questions.explanation: Plan composition can span agents while their detailed settings remain in the documented administration surfaces.

options.text: Clone agent settings into private plan records.
Require separate plans because rollout manager cannot group enabled agents under one rollout.
Replace the agents existing administrator configuration with manual target edits during activation.
Use one multi-agent rollout plan and the existing settings.

optionExplanations.o1: The manager uses existing settings without duplicating controls.
optionExplanations.o2: A single plan may cover multiple agents.
optionExplanations.o3: The documented design retains corresponding agent administration settings.
optionExplanations.o4: The plan can cover both enabled agents without duplicating configuration authority.

questions.prompt: A team needs editable configuration in development and a controlled deployment artifact for preproduction. Which packaging approach follows the Contact Center ALM recommendation?
questions.answer: Author in an unmanaged source solution and export a managed solution for the target.
questions.explanation: Maintain an editable source configuration and distribute its managed export to target environments.

options.text: Build directly in a managed solution in production and export it to development.
Author in an unmanaged source solution and export a managed solution for the target.
Import the unmanaged development solution as the permanent production customization layer.
Keep separate handwritten configuration in every target environment.

optionExplanations.o1: This reverses the recommended source-to-target flow.
optionExplanations.o2: Source authoring remains editable while the target receives a managed artifact.
optionExplanations.o3: The recommendation is a managed export for the target.
optionExplanations.o4: Independent target changes weaken source-controlled deployment.

questions.prompt: A release lead is preparing the next managed Contact Center configuration update. The team wants a repeatable deployment that allows later changes to arrive from development. Which TWO actions belong in this release policy? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Keep source and target installed solution versions in parity. Deliver managed configuration changes through managed solution imports.
questions.explanation: Check platform-solution parity and keep update ownership in managed releases.

options.text: Allow local target edits as the normal source of future configuration changes.
Ignore installed solution versions if the configuration names match.
Keep source and target installed solution versions in parity.
Import the release as unmanaged to suppress all active customizations automatically.
Deliver managed configuration changes through managed solution imports.

optionExplanations.o1: Local target edits create active customizations and undermine later updates.
optionExplanations.o2: Names do not establish the documented version parity.
optionExplanations.o3: Version parity is an explicit import prerequisite.
optionExplanations.o4: An unmanaged import is not the documented managed-update approach.
optionExplanations.o5: The documented approach keeps changes in managed imports.

questions.prompt: A managed configuration was imported, then edited directly in the target. A later managed release imports successfully, but the target still behaves according to the local edit. Which explanation best fits the documented ALM behavior?
questions.answer: The active customization can take precedence over the managed update.
questions.explanation: Successful import and effective runtime values can diverge when a target active customization remains above the managed layer.

options.text: A successful import guarantees that the newest managed values override every local customization.
A newer managed solution always takes precedence over the active local layer solely because its version increased.
The solution version inventory alone determines runtime property values, independent of component layers.
The active customization can take precedence over the managed update.

optionExplanations.o1: Import success does not override an active layer that masks the managed values.
optionExplanations.o2: The documented active layer can mask future managed configuration updates.
optionExplanations.o3: Installed versions do not remove the active-layer precedence described for this case.
optionExplanations.o4: An active layer can mask later imported managed changes.

questions.prompt: A retired configuration exists only because a managed solution supplied it. The team has assessed that solution contents and dependencies and approved its removal. Which cleanup path does the Contact Center guidance prescribe?
questions.answer: Delete the managed solution that introduced the configuration.
questions.explanation: Managed ownership determines the documented removal operation. The solution impact assessment in the stem is essential to this cleanup decision.

options.text: Delete the managed solution that introduced the configuration.
Delete the target managed configuration record directly using a bulk record deletion operation.
Remove only an active customization and assume that also uninstalls the underlying managed configuration.
Remove the component from an unmanaged target container and assume its managed ownership disappears.

optionExplanations.o1: Removal is performed through the supplying managed solution.
optionExplanations.o2: The guide does not allow target record-level deletion of imported managed configuration.
optionExplanations.o3: Removing an override is not the documented removal of the supplying managed configuration.
optionExplanations.o4: Unmanaged container membership does not delete the supplying managed solution ownership.

questions.prompt: A migration plan uses the documented channel configuration procedure. Templates, skill rules, new capacity profiles, queues, and workstreams are in the procedure work package. Which TWO additional work packages must be planned separately because the procedure explicitly excludes them? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Channel provider and account setup. Agent configuration plus AI and analytics settings.
questions.explanation: Migration scope is a deployment boundary: channel configuration movement does not establish readiness of the excluded integrations and services.

options.text: Channel provider and account setup.
Session and notification template configuration.
Queue configuration.
Agent configuration plus AI and analytics settings.
New capacity profile configuration.

optionExplanations.o1: These are explicitly excluded from the documented scope.
optionExplanations.o2: Templates are listed in the migration sequence.
optionExplanations.o3: Queues are included in that sequence.
optionExplanations.o4: These settings are explicitly outside the procedure scope.
optionExplanations.o5: New capacity profiles are included in the sequence.

questions.prompt: A migration runbook imports channel workstreams first and plans to import their templates, skill rules, capacity profiles, and queues afterward. Permissions and custom schema are already ready. What change aligns the runbook with the documented dependency sequence?
questions.answer: Move the documented dependencies before channel workstreams/settings.
questions.explanation: Import foundational routing configuration before channel workstreams and settings, then verify the assembled target.

options.text: Verify workstreams before their dependencies arrive.
Import all channel workstreams before importing queues and template dependencies.
Move the documented dependencies before channel workstreams/settings.
Skip template migration when names already match.

optionExplanations.o1: Verification follows the assembled configuration, not missing dependencies.
optionExplanations.o2: This retains the reversed dependency sequence.
optionExplanations.o3: Templates, skills, profiles and queues precede channel workstreams/settings.
optionExplanations.o4: Matching names do not replace the documented configuration migration.

questions.prompt: A channel migration imported skill-based rules and capacity profiles, and the target rules render without errors. Intended representative accounts and roles exist. Before accepting their skill/profile-based assignments, which additional target verification work does the documented procedure call for?
questions.answer: Establish the target user/resource skill and capacity-profile associations.
questions.explanation: Configuration import success leaves target user/resource associations as a separate verification responsibility.

options.text: Reimport unchanged workstreams and treat error-free rendering as proof of representative readiness.
Establish the target user/resource skill and capacity-profile associations.
Raise the default capacity limits and assume the relevant user/profile associations then exist.
Treat matching source and target ruleset names as sufficient without checking user/resource links.

optionExplanations.o1: Rendering checks do not establish the required target user/resource associations.
optionExplanations.o2: Verification explicitly requires these target associations.
optionExplanations.o3: A higher limit does not establish the required associations.
optionExplanations.o4: Names do not establish the manual linking, association or creation steps in verification.

questions.prompt: A team needs a test environment containing schema and customizations but no source business data. It will create its own channels and workstreams after the documented channel reset step. Which copy choice matches the plan?
questions.answer: Minimal copy, with the documented channel preparation.
questions.explanation: Choose the copy scope based on data needs; minimal copy requires its documented channel preparation.

options.text: Full copy, retaining source business data.
Minimal copy, leaving channels unchanged and assuming copied business data is available for testing.
Managed solution import alone, treating that operation as a copy of the entire source environment.
Minimal copy, with the documented channel preparation.

optionExplanations.o1: A full copy includes source data.
optionExplanations.o2: Minimal copy excludes source data and requires documented channel preparation.
optionExplanations.o3: A solution import is not the requested environment-copy option.
optionExplanations.o4: Minimal copy copies schema/customizations without source data and has documented channel follow-up.

questions.prompt: After a full omnichannel environment copy, the team prepares an isolated target website and target record routing. Other channel integrations are already reviewed. Which TWO actions address these specific target requirements? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Replace the website snippet with the target-generated chat snippet. Configure and validate record routing separately in the target.
questions.explanation: Website integration and record routing each need their own target action; a full Dataverse copy is not an acceptance test for either.

options.text: Keep the source website snippet because both environments contain similarly named workstreams.
Replace the website snippet with the target-generated chat snippet.
Assume record-routing configuration is supported by the copy and skip its target configuration.
Use source credentials as proof that target routing works.
Configure and validate record routing separately in the target.

optionExplanations.o1: The source snippet targets the source integration.
optionExplanations.o2: The copied target generates its own widget configuration.
optionExplanations.o3: The documentation excludes supported copying of record-routing configuration.
optionExplanations.o4: Credential reuse does not validate target routing.
optionExplanations.o5: The documented copy guidance calls for separate target configuration and validation.

questions.prompt: A full copy of an existing ACS-backed voice environment leaves the target referencing the source ACS resource. The source must keep serving its users. Which target plan follows the copy guidance?
questions.answer: Replace the copied target ACS reference with target-specific voice resources.
questions.explanation: Isolate the target ACS integration while preserving the source. This concerns an existing copied configuration, not availability of new standalone ACS provisioning.

options.text: Replace the copied target ACS reference with target-specific voice resources.
Share the source ACS resource between the two environments.
Disconnect the source and keep the target reference unchanged.
Rename the target workstream and keep the shared ACS resource.

optionExplanations.o1: The guidance requires environment-specific resource and number configuration.
optionExplanations.o2: A resource can be used in one environment only under this guidance.
optionExplanations.o3: This does not provide the target-specific integration and jeopardizes the source requirement.
optionExplanations.o4: A workstream rename does not correct the environment-specific external resource dependency.

questions.prompt: A copied Microsoft Teams messaging account still references the source agent/application. The target must operate independently. Which remediation follows the environment-copy guidance?
questions.answer: Recreate the target Teams channel and its target associations.
questions.explanation: Review external associations after copying; copied messaging records can retain a source agent/application dependency.

options.text: Keep the copied messaging account and change only its workstream association while retaining the source agent/application reference.
Publish a target agent but keep the copied messaging account linked to the source application.
Recreate the target Teams channel and its target associations.
Reauthenticate the source-associated messaging account and treat that as a recreated target channel.

optionExplanations.o1: Changing only the workstream leaves the cross-environment messaging-account dependency.
optionExplanations.o2: Agent publishing alone does not recreate the target-specific Teams messaging account/channel.
optionExplanations.o3: Recreation and target associations remove the copied source dependency.
optionExplanations.o4: Refreshing authentication alone is not the documented target channel recreation and association process.

questions.prompt: An omnichannel copy includes a Copilot agent configuration. All target channel resources and user permissions are ready. Before accepting agent escalation in the target, which TWO actions belong to the documented agent checks? Choose TWO.
questions.answer: Review connections/authentication and associate workstreams with the intended target agent. Publish the agent and test escalation and routing scenarios in the target.
questions.explanation: Validate the target agent dependencies, then publish and exercise its escalation path.

options.text: Treat copied agent capability records as proof that target connections and authentication are valid.
Publish the copied agent without checking which target workstreams or connections it uses.
Review connections/authentication and associate workstreams with the intended target agent.
Validate only agent authoring availability and omit escalation and routing tests after publishing.
Publish the agent and test escalation and routing scenarios in the target.

optionExplanations.o1: Copied configuration must still be checked for source-environment dependencies.
optionExplanations.o2: Publication alone does not validate the required environment-specific associations.
optionExplanations.o3: Target associations and environment-specific settings must be reviewed.
